feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications roles: the progression at NACo is clear, the scope is substantial, and the profile aligns well with the target title. Writing is polished overall, but impact would improve with more outcome-focused metrics, less repetition across skills sections, and a few consistency edits.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression and credibility: multiple promotions at one organization strongly signal trust, growth, and leadership.  
- Good scope and relevance: combines strategy, web/CMS, analytics, multimedia, and governance in a way that fits modern digital leadership roles.  
- Generally strong writing: concise, professional, and easy to follow, with solid examples such as the 10,000+ page migration and in-house studio build.

1. Top improvements  
- Add sharper results: several bullets describe responsibilities more than outcomes. Include measurable impact where possible (engagement growth, efficiency gains, revenue/supporter impact, adoption rates).  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating would improve structure and scannability.  
- Fix minor style/grammar consistency issues: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “12 years of experience”; use consistent serial commas (“web, email, social, and multimedia” vs “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”); “A2/Learning” is stylistically awkward—prefer “French: A2 (learning).”
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear positioning, but it reads slightly generic and repeats themes covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening the language and anchoring it more directly to senior digital leadership will increase impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner, standard CV phrasing.
- Lead with your senior value proposition: digital strategy, platform modernization, and operational leadership for mission-driven/public-sector organizations.
- Reduce the long channel list or compress it into “multi-channel digital communications” to avoid sounding repetitive.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading multi-channel programs across web, email, social, and multimedia. Brings deep expertise in digital strategy, platform modernization, and the workflows, governance, and systems that enable effective communications in complex, mission-driven organizations. Strong track record in advocacy messaging, stakeholder alignment, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications” and workflow/systems language overlap heavily with Core Competencies.
- Advocacy, stakeholder coordination, and accessible content also reappear in Topline Skills and work experience.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. It would be more effective if tightened to emphasize higher-level strengths rather than repeating detailed skill categories listed elsewhere.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace broad or repetitive phrases with sharper, senior-level terms: “Digital transformation leadership,” “Editorial systems & governance,” “CMS modernization,” “Analytics & performance reporting.”
- Standardize style and parallel structure; use mostly noun phrases and avoid mixing “communication” with “coordination” and “production” inconsistently.
- Prioritize the most marketable, recent strengths tied to target roles: digital strategy, platform modernization, governance, analytics, advocacy messaging, and multimedia.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital transformation leadership • Multi-channel communications strategy • CMS administration & web operations • Editorial systems & governance • Analytics & performance reporting • Workflow architecture & process improvement • Cross-functional stakeholder leadership • Policy & advocacy communications • Multimedia & live event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section substantially duplicates the header and Topline Skills; consider shortening it or removing lower-value items like “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination.”
- “Workflow design” and “systems architecture” are close enough to consolidate.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, competencies, and project footer. Tighten it around 3–4 highest-impact contributions and add outcomes or scale.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper lead: “Embedded as a full-time strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading web modernization, campaign delivery, and AI-enabled content discovery.”
- Replace generic verbs (“support,” “advise,” “deliver”) with ownership verbs: led, built, launched, redesigned, standardized, improved.
- Consolidate bullets into impact areas: Drupal campaign/microsite builds; communications systems/workflows/analytics; governance across channels; AI search initiative.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: site traffic, number of publishers/teams supported, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, reduction in publishing time, search success/discovery improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search initiative” overlaps with the Recent Projects footer; keep one concise mention here and let the footer hold technical detail.
- “Governance, workflows, analytics” repeats prior NACo roles; emphasize what is new in this consulting engagement.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It will be stronger if you tighten the opening, foreground the biggest outcomes, and avoid repeating channel-management details covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit
- Replace the broad lead sentence with a sharper scope/outcome line: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Lead with the website modernization as the anchor achievement: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel oversight more outcome-based: add growth, engagement, deliverability, production volume, or campaign impact if available; otherwise shorten.
- Tighten remaining bullets to action + result: “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio, increasing capacity for advocacy programming, event production, and recurring multimedia content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this item focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video-programming language may duplicate older NACo entries unless framed here as studio buildout and scaled operational capacity.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this item reads broad and overlaps with both the later Director role and the earlier Digital Media Manager/Producer role. Tighten it around scope, channel ownership, and systems/process impact at this level.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize operational ownership: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial execution and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Combine related bullets and sharpen verbs: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more outcome-focused: “Launched and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Clarify cross-functional/process impact: “Built stronger editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving coordination and content consistency.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital publishing workflows” and “editorial coordination” overlap with the Director role’s governance/planning language; keep this item more execution-focused.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this entry as scaling/formalizing the program.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this skills block is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. It should sharpen the candidate’s differentiators and use tighter, less repetitive phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with more distinctive, outcome-oriented wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy for high-volume public-sector platforms
- Editorial governance, publishing workflows, and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership across web, email, social, and video
- Advocacy and public-sector messaging for member and stakeholder audiences
- Audience-centered content strategy, planning, and information design
- Consider dropping “leadership” and “planning” where implied; the section reads stronger with concrete capability nouns.
- If space allows, align wording to recent work: emphasize governance, platform modernization, and audience discovery over broad “messaging.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” repeat the header/Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” also duplicates language already established across recent NACo roles.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw keyword dump and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should be tighter, more strategic, and emphasize the most relevant recent strengths.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led wording, e.g.: “Drupal and CMS modernization • Front-end web implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Prioritize recent/relevant platforms: keep Drupal first; consider dropping WordPress, SharePoint, and Power Pages here unless they are important for target roles.
- Replace vague phrasing like “technical execution” with stronger, outcome-oriented language such as “web platforms, integrations, and automation.”
- If space allows, add one impact cue tied to recent work, e.g. “enterprise Drupal modernization” or “search and discovery systems.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current list duplicates the detailed platform/tool inventory already covered in “Technical + IT.”
- “CMS modernization,” “workflow automation,” and “AI-enabled search experiences” also overlap with Core Competencies; keep this section more platform/execution-focused.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list for a senior digital leader, but it reads as a generic keyword dump. It should emphasize strategic analytics capability and avoid repeating the near-identical “Technical + IT” analytics list.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Analytics strategy, reporting & optimization.”
- Tighten and group items: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework design • executive/leadership reporting • SEO and digital performance analysis”
- Consider replacing “Leadership reporting” with “Executive reporting” or “Decision-ready reporting” for sharper phrasing.
- If space allows, add one outcome-oriented qualifier tied to recent work, e.g. “analytics infrastructure for enterprise web modernization” or “measurement for high-traffic public-sector platforms.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies: Analytics and reporting infrastructure” and “Technical + IT: Data, Analytics & Optimization.”
- “SEO and performance analysis” may duplicate broader optimization language elsewhere unless positioned as a distinct specialty.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and older NACo bullets. Tighten it to emphasize higher-level production capability and recent leadership-level relevance rather than listing generic tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from task list to capability statement: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera and studio system operation • Virtual event production workflows”
- Consider replacing “Video production and editing” with “Broadcast-quality video production” to align with the in-house studio achievement in the 2022–2024 role.
- Combine “Livestreaming” and “Hybrid and virtual event production” into one stronger phrase to reduce fragmentation.
- If space allows, add scale/context rather than tools alone, e.g. “Studio and livestream operations for advocacy programming and member events.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies; vary wording or remove one.
- “Studio operations” and “PTZ camera systems” are quite tactical for a senior profile unless balanced with delivery/leadership language.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Since Drupal is the strongest and most recent platform in the experience section, lead with that and de-emphasize lower-signal tools.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add light qualifiers to show depth: **Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Consider renaming the heading to **CMS & Web Platforms** for cleaner phrasing.
- If you want more impact, replace this list with a tighter version: **Drupal (advanced), WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates the Topline Skills entry “Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists Drupal, WordPress, and SharePoint.
- Avoid adding “CMS modernization” here; that concept is already covered elsewhere and is stronger in Core Competencies/Topline Skills.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools that support recent Drupal, analytics, and automation work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Front-End & Technical Implementation**
- Rewrite as: **HTML5/CSS3 • JavaScript/jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions**
- Drop version numbers unless they matter; **HTML/CSS** is cleaner than **HTML5/CSS3**.
- If accurate, add one higher-signal qualifier in parentheses, e.g. **API integrations (REST/JSON)** or **GitHub Actions (deployment automation)** to show practical depth.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- **HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery • API integrations** already appears in **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; keep the fuller phrasing in one place only.
- Consider whether **Google Tag Manager** fits better under **Data, Analytics & Optimization** to reduce category blur.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow design capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to **Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools** to better match the tools listed.
- Group by function for faster scanning: **Automation:** Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | **Project/Work Management:** Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | **Collaboration:** Slack, Teams.
- If accurate, add light qualifiers tied to recent work: e.g., **Airtable (workflow databases), Power Automate/Zapier (cross-platform automations), Jira/Asana (editorial and delivery tracking)**.
- Consider trimming to the strongest, most relevant tools from recent roles; if Basecamp or Trello are older/less used, remove them.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills; keep this section tool-focused, not conceptual.
- Slack and Teams are common collaboration tools; include only if they were central to workflow/system design.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The item is clear but too bare to add much value on its own. Since email leadership already appears in recent NACo roles, this line should stay tool-focused and, if possible, reflect level of use rather than repeat channel ownership.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add qualifiers for depth: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (campaign automation) • Higher Logic (member email/community communications) • Mailchimp (newsletter deployment)**
- Keep it platform-only; avoid adding responsibilities like “managed newsletters” here since those are stronger in Work Experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Engagement” overlaps with broader communications claims in Core Competencies and Work Experience; “Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms” is more precise.
- Don’t add audience size or newsletter volume here; those metrics are already better placed in the NACo experience bullets.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with clearer scope and any measurable outputs.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe around early-team building and hands-on production: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital media function…”
- Tighten phrasing and reduce channel list repetition: “improved publishing workflows and supported web, email, social, and video operations.”
- Add concrete outputs if available: number of livestreams/events supported, cadence of weekly videos, audience growth, or size/timing of the website refresh.
- Possible rewrite: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital media team, improving publishing workflows and supporting web, email, social, and video operations. Contributed to a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and provided day-to-day oversight for a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on launching/producing the format, not expanding it.
- “strengthening workflows across web, email, social” is repeated elsewhere; emphasize first-team buildout and execution.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a notable “first podcast” achievement, but it reads broadly and overlaps with later multimedia/digital roles. Tighten it to emphasize coordination, cross-functional support, and the launch outcome.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the strongest differentiator: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county-focused programs and policy priorities.”
- Make the podcast launch the second sentence and sharpen ownership: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, production coordination, and rollout.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials” with a more specific verb: “supported digital and multimedia content for program and policy communications.”
- If possible, add one measurable detail: number of episodes launched, audience/downloads, or number/type of projects supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later Digital Media Manager/Producer and Associate Communications Director entries; keep this item lighter on generic multimedia language.
- Avoid overstating digital leadership here since stronger, more recent leadership evidence appears in 2018–2024 roles.
